heading: INT. FLOODED MINE ELEVATOR CAGE - NIGHT

units.text: INT. FLOODED MINE ELEVATOR CAGE - NIGHT
A rusted lift hangs in a shaft of black water, rising and falling an inch with some far-off tide.
The headlamp of INSPECTOR WILHELMINA SORVOLD (40s, canvas coveralls) throws a shaking coin of light across the wet iron.

Beside her, huddled against the bars, sits her brother-in-law GUNNAR ASKELAND (50s, a missing front tooth), and across from them, curled on the floor in a miner's oilskin, a girl no one hired: TILDA (12, bare feet, eyes too steady).
She keeps the lamp low.
He keeps his hands over his mouth.
They both watch the girl, who watches the water.
She hums.
It is a lullaby, and it is slightly wrong.
Where did you come from?
units.name: WILHELMINA

units.text: Down.
units.name: TILDA

units.text: He laughs once, a dry sound with no air in it, and she turns the light on him until he stops.
Wilma, the cable.
units.name: GUNNAR

units.text: She follows his stare.
The cable above them is not rusting.
It is wet, and moving, and not metal.
She draws a slow breath.
He crosses himself with a shaking hand.
The girl smiles, takes the lamp gently from her, and switches it off.
Now you can hear it.
units.name: TILDA
